The '''2014 [[Tippeligaen]]''' was the 70th completed season of top division [[association football|football]] in Norway. The competition began on 28 March 2014, two weeks later than in the [[2013 Tippeligaen|previous season]]. A three-week summer-break in June was scheduled due to the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]], and the decisive match was played on 9 November 2014.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.dagbladet.no/2013/11/15/sport/tippeligaen/fotball/30345525/ |language=no |title=Tippeligaen starter 30. mars i 2014 |newspaper=Dagbladet |first=Gorm S. |last=Andersen |date=15 November 2013 |access-date=19 November 2013}}</ref> [[Strømsgodset Toppfotball|Strømsgodset]] were the defending champions. [[FK Bodø/Glimt|Bodø/Glimt]] and [[Stabæk Fotball|Stabæk]] joined as the promoted clubs from the [[2013 1. divisjon]]. They replaced [[Tromsø IL|Tromsø]] and [[Hønefoss BK|Hønefoss]] who were relegated to the [[2014 1. divisjon]].

[[Molde FK|Molde]] won their third title, with four matches to spare following a 2–1 away win against [[Viking FK|Viking]] on 4 October 2014.<ref name="league champions">{{cite web|url=https://www.dagbladet.no/sport/molde-er-seriemester-2014/60962232 |title=– Vi skal ta cupen og Moldes poengrekord |website=www.tv2.no |publisher=[[TV2 (Norway)|TV2]]|language=no|date=24 September 2016|access-date=5 December 2019}}</ref> The team broke the record for most points (71) and most wins (22).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tv2.no/a/8613576/ |title=Molde er seriemester 2014 |website=www.dagbladet.no |publisher=[[Dagbladet]]|language=no|date=4 October 2014|access-date=5 December 2019}}</ref>

==Overview==
===Summary===
On 4 October, Molde were confirmed as league champions following their 2–1 away win against [[Viking FK|Viking]] in the 26th round.<ref name="league champions"/> They won their third title. On 2 November, in the penultimate round of the season, [[Sandnes Ulf]] were the first team to be relegated to the 1. divisjon when they gave away a 3–1 lead in stoppage time and drew 3–3 away to [[IK Start|Start]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tv2.no/a/6189052/ |title=Sandnes Ulf rykket ned etter utrolig kollaps |website=tv2.no |publisher=[[TV2 (Norway)|TV2]] |language=no |date=2 November 2014 |access-date=5 December 2019}}</ref> On the final day, [[Sogndal Fotball|Sogndal]] were relegated and [[SK Brann|Brann]] qualified for the relegation play-offs. On 26 November, Brann were the third team to be relegated after losing the play-offs 4–1 on aggregate against [[Mjøndalen IF|Mjøndalen]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tv2.no/a/6279916/ |title=Brann rykket ned etter å ha blitt ydmyket av Mjøndalen |website=tv2.no |publisher=[[TV2 (Norway)|TV2]] |language=no |date=26 November 2014 |access-date=5 December 2019}}</ref>

==Teams==
The league was contested by 16 teams: the best 13 teams of the 2013 season, and the 14th-placed [[Sarpsborg 08 FF|Sarpsborg 08]] who won the relegation-playoffs against [[Ranheim Fotball|Ranheim]], in addition to two promoted teams from [[2013 1. divisjon|1. divisjon]]. The promoted teams were [[FK Bodø/Glimt|Bodø/Glimt]] and [[Stabæk Fotball|Stabæk]], returning to the top flight after an absence of four years and one season respectively. They replaced [[Tromsø IL|Tromsø]] (after an eleven-year spell in Eliteserien) and [[Hønefoss BK|Hønefoss]] (relegated after two seasons presence).

==Relegation play-offs==
{{main|2014 Eliteserien promotion/relegation play-offs}}

The 14th-placed team, [[SK Brann|Brann]], took part in a two-legged play-off against [[Mjøndalen IF|Mjøndalen]], the winners of the 2014 1. divisjon [[2014 1. divisjon#Promotion play-offs|promotion play-offs]], to decide who would play in the [[2015 Tippeligaen]].
